decisions.decision: Applied the pre-registered pilot rule verbatim and did NOT buy the round.
decisions.rationale: N=3 is the rule's explicit CEILING HELD branch. A decision rule reinterpreted after seeing the numbers is not a decision rule. The verdict distribution (2 genuinely_red + 1 blunt_red) is recorded second and is explicitly not the gate.

decisions.decision: Recorded the outcome in a NEW targets.json pilot_result field instead of editing ceiling_note.
decisions.rationale: pilot_decision_rule forbids editing itself after the pilot runs; adding a sibling field preserves the audit trail byte-for-byte. Both protected fields were verified identical to HEAD by parse-and-compare.

decisions.decision: Reached both close-out verdicts BY the dedicated agents, refusing the workflows' inline short-circuits.
decisions.rationale: Both short-circuits would have passed cleanly -- and the nyquist auditor then found a real coverage gap the short-circuit would have missed entirely. Self-certification is not an audit.

decisions.decision: Corrected the living status records but did NOT rewrite historical SUMMARYs.
decisions.rationale: A SUMMARY is a point-in-time record; 21-04 was true when written. Editing it to tidy a status field would falsify history. A clearly marked forward-pointer addendum carries the new information instead.

decisions.decision: Reconciled EVL-03 only, and flagged EVL-01/EVL-02 as unverified rather than sweeping them along.
decisions.rationale: They were not re-verified in that pass. Fixing one row is not evidence about the others, and silently widening scope would have manufactured confidence.

context_notes: THE HEADLINE IS THAT A PRE-REGISTERED $4.11 PILOT KILLED A $27 ROUND, AND THAT IS A WIN, NOT A DISAPPOINTMENT. The cell is at a structural ceiling: the baseline arm loads a skill that already contains the answer, so nothing can be measured there. The discipline that made it usable was committing the decision rule BEFORE the pilot ran, then applying it without reinterpretation once N was visible. SECOND, THE AUDITS EARNED THEIR KEEP. Both workflows offered an inline short-circuit that would have passed phase 21 cleanly; both were refused per the never-self-certify rule, and the nyquist auditor then found that 2 of 5 own-skill arms had never been parity-asserted -- the phase requirement said 'all THREE arms', so the letter passed while the intent failed after the instrument grew. Requirements pin a number; instruments grow. THIRD, THE AUDITOR'S FIX FAILED ITS OWN MUTATION TEST BEFORE IT PASSED, which is exactly why it is trustworthy. A green check that has never been shown to fail is not evidence -- drive every important assertion in both directions. FOURTH, A RED RESULT WAS MY OWN FAULT AND I NEARLY MISREAD IT: a battery failed on the leftover-worktree canary because I had killed a duplicate run mid-crux and its teardown never ran. Diagnose a failure to its cause before doubting the thing under test. I also wrote a fail-open check this session (test $? placed after an echo, which always passes) -- that is a recurrence in this project, so treat exit-status gating as muscle memory, not a rule to recall. FIFTH, ON RECORD-KEEPING: a status field only ever written by the step that DEFERS it will never be cleared by the step that RESOLVES it. That is why EVL-03 sat 'Pending' for a week after its round completed. Build-then-halt needs a matching reconcile-on-completion action. And when reconciling, correct LIVING records and leave HISTORY alone.
